blocks.content: Rotation is Earth's spinning movement on its axis from west to east. Because of this direction, the Sun appears to move east to west.

cells: 23h 56m — time taken relative to distant stars.
24h — time taken for the Sun to reappear at the same position.

blocks.content: A Sidereal Day is shorter than a Solar Day because the Earth must rotate slightly more than 360 degrees to complete one full solar day.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Earth rotates on its axis from West to East, completing one rotation relative to fixed distant stars in 23 hours, 56 minutes, and 4 seconds.
A Sidereal Day is approximately 4 minutes shorter than a Solar Day because Earth revolves around the Sun while rotating on its axis.
Rotation causes the diurnal cycle of day and night, separated by the Circle of Illumination.
The Coriolis Force, generated by Earth's rotation, causes atmospheric winds and ocean currents to deflect.
Centrifugal force from rotation causes Earth's oblate spheroid shape, bulging at the equator and flattening at the poles.

blocks.content: While Earth rotates, it also moves along its orbit. Therefore, it must rotate slightly more than 360° for the Sun to appear in the same position — making the solar day longer.

items: Exact duration of Sidereal Day (23 hours, 56 minutes, 4 seconds) is frequently tested in UPSC and SSC Prelims.
Direction of Earth's rotation is West to East (counter-clockwise when viewed from above the North Pole).
Ferrel's Law and Coriolis Effect deflect winds to the right in the Northern Hemisphere and left in the Southern Hemisphere.
